findings.title: Dependency observations read function/class-level data, against the architecture and the slice's own success criteria
findings.description:
Section 6 says "Function- and class-level edge endpoints are resolved to their owning file's layer rather than dropped, so a `calls` edge between two functions in different layers still counts." This conflicts with:
- The architecture's read discipline (`360-arch…md:107-110`: "function- and class-level nodes are not read").
- The slice's own Success Criterion 9 (`:332-333`: "no function- or class-level node is read").
- Walkthrough step 7 (`:424`).
- The same paragraph's first sentence, which limits the section to inter-layer `imports` and `depends_on`.
- The mapping table row 6 (`:179`), which lists only `edges[]` fields.

The mechanism is also missing. The verified-facts table (`:99`) suggests only file, config and pipeline nodes carry `filePath`. So finding a function's "owning file" means either parsing type-prefixed IDs (`function:path:name`, where the path can contain colons) or walking `contains` edges. The design specifies neither.

**Fix:** drop the function/class endpoint resolution and keep 361's file-level `imports`/`depends_on` scope. If the `calls` signal really is needed, raise it as an architecture change rather than a slice decision.

Separately, SC9 should say what it actually means: no function- or class-node content enters context. Correction 1's cross-check must look up node `type` for every `nodeIds` entry, so it necessarily touches those nodes inside `jq`.

findings.title: File-level selector contradicts itself and inverts the architecture's allow-list
findings.description:
Line 151 says the selector "becomes an explicit type allow-list". Lines 155-158 then define an exclusion (`.type != "function" and .type != "class"`) and say it is "Stated as an exclusion rather than an allow-list deliberately." An implementer cannot satisfy both.

The exclusion also departs from the architecture, which names nine file-level types as an allow-list (`360-arch…md:108-109`). Its rationale works against the architecture's drift posture ("must surface as a loud failure", `:134-136`):
- If a future upstream release adds a sub-file type such as `method`, `interface` or `variable`, the exclusion pulls it silently into context.
- The only guard is the "no `filePath`" check, which misses any such type that carries `filePath`.

**Fix:** select the architecture's nine types, and report any node type outside nine ∪ {`function`, `class`} as upstream drift. New types then fail loudly in both directions instead of failing open.

Correction 1 has a related gap: when the cross-check finds a function or class entry in `nodeIds`, the design doesn't say whether the reported layer count includes it.

findings.title: "Closing observations" reopen the path to untraceable claims, and the example is a hallucination trap
findings.description:
The governing rule (`:186-189`) says no section is ever "filled with prose that is not traceable to its named fields." Section-closing observations are then allowed if they are "derivable from the table directly above". But the example given, "complexity concentrates in the seams where squadron meets an external SDK", fails that test:
- No graph field identifies "external SDK seams".
- It is an interpretation of `summary` text, which is exactly what `[INFERRED]` exists to mark.

So the test is not mechanical, and the example shows it already being failed. If the example sentence goes into the skill text, a model with thin data will copy it (CLAUDE.md, "Hallucination traps in prompts").

**Fix:** either drop closing observations, or limit them to restating counts and distributions already shown, such as "N of M complex files are in layer X". Don't put a sample sentence in the skill.

findings.title: Failure modes for the three new coverage inputs are not separated
findings.description:
Section 7 adds three new reads: `meta.json` `analyzedFiles`, `config.json` and `.understandignore`. The mapping table (`:180`) gives a single fallback, "`[GAP: ...]` naming the unreadable file". That merges cases that need different handling:

- **Absent `.understandignore` or `config.json`:** both are optional upstream files, so absence is probably the normal default state, not a gap. The design covers neither case.
- **Unparseable `config.json`, or non-integer `analyzedFiles`:** 361 gives "unparseable" its own message for the graph. Here it isn't addressed.
- **`.understandignore` paragraph:** it contradicts itself. "An all-comments file (this repo's current state has 17 active lines) is reported as 'defaults only'". The parenthetical describes a file that is not all-comments.

**Fix:** for each of the three inputs, state the output for:
- absent;
- present but unreadable or unparseable;
- present and empty (or all comments).

Then rewrite the `.understandignore` sentence.

findings.title: Interfaces table and verified facts list fields the mapping never uses
findings.description:
These fields appear in the tables but not in the binding mapping table:
- `edges[].direction`
- `nodes[].tags` for "section grouping"
- `tour[].languageLesson` (measured at `:106`)

Either map them or delete the rows, so implementers don't build reads that nothing uses.

findings.title: Walkthrough gaps in the tamper and full-slice steps
findings.description:
- **Step 5:** it creates `kg-empty-tour.json` and `kg-no-entrypoints.json` but never says to swap them in as `knowledge-graph.json`, which is the only file the skill reads. `$S` is never defined.
- **Step 8:** it diffs against `main` instead of the configured integration target.
- **`ruff format --check`:** adds nothing when no Python changes.

findings.title: "Explicitly deferred by 361" cannot be traced to the 361 design
findings.description: The 361 slice design does not mention `config.json`, `.understandignore` or `analyzedFiles`. The coverage section is still justified by the architecture (`360-arch…md:86-89`). Cite that instead, or cite wherever 361's skill text records the deferral.

findings.title: Small inconsistency about which files change
findings.description: The Overview says "Everything here is markdown edits to the existing `commands/analysis/understand.md`." Technical Decisions and SC11 (`:336-338`) also edit `user/reference/analyze-codebase-prompt.md`, and SC11 calls it a "non-document file" even though it lives under `project-documents/`. Change the wording to match.
